description: Comprehensive question bank on Karnataka Agriculture based on Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26 and related sources. Covers all topics from the provided PDF notes.
subject: Karnataka Agriculture

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What do agriculture and allied activities support in Karnataka?

options.B: Rural livelihoods, food and raw materials, employment, inputs to agro-based industries, and economic and social stability

questions.explanation: Agriculture and allied activities support rural livelihoods, provide food and raw materials, generate employment, supply inputs to agro-based industries and contribute to the State's economic and social stability.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an allied agricultural activity?
questions.explanation: Allied activities include livestock rearing, dairy, poultry, sheep and goat rearing, fisheries, sericulture, apiculture and horticulture. Steel manufacturing is an industrial activity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Why is Karnataka suitable for diverse agricultural production?

options.B: Varied rainfall, temperature, altitude, soils and landforms

questions.explanation: Karnataka has varied rainfall, temperature, altitude, soils and landforms, ranging from the humid coastal belt and Western Ghats to the semi-arid Deccan plateau and irrigated river valleys.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What are the three main agricultural seasons in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The three main agricultural seasons in Karnataka are Kharif, Rabi and Summer.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: When are Kharif crops generally sown in Karnataka?

options.C: June to July with the onset of South-West Monsoon

questions.explanation: Kharif crops are generally sown with the onset of the South-West Monsoon, mainly from June to July, and harvested from September to December depending on the crop.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: When are Rabi crops generally harvested in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops are generally sown after the monsoon, mainly from October to December, and harvested from February to April.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Summer crops in Karnataka are generally cultivated between which months?
questions.explanation: Summer crops are generally cultivated between February and May, often with irrigation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the average total cropped area in Karnataka from 2020-21 to 2024-25 according to the Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26 reports an average total cropped area of 111.99 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the average Kharif cropped area in Karnataka from 2020-21 to 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The average Kharif cropped area was 82.25 lakh hectares, Rabi 23.64 lakh hectares and Summer 6.09 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the average Rabi cropped area in Karnataka from 2020-21 to 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The average Rabi cropped area was 23.64 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the average Summer cropped area in Karnataka from 2020-21 to 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The average Summer cropped area was 6.09 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the estimated total area under major crops in Karnataka in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The estimated total area under major crops in 2024-25 was 112.09 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the area under food grains in Karnataka in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: In 2024-25, 85.71 lakh hectares were under food grains.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the estimated food-grain production in Karnataka in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: The estimated food-grain production in 2024-25 was 151.57 lakh tonnes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: According to the Second Advance Estimates for 2025-26, what was the total major crop area in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Total major crop area was estimated at 107.1 lakh hectares for 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: According to the Second Advance Estimates for 2025-26, what was the area under food grains in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Food grains occupied 78.6 lakh hectares according to the Second Advance Estimates for 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the estimated food production in Karnataka according to the Second Advance Estimates for 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Estimated food production was 136.22 lakh tonnes according to the Second Advance Estimates for 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What proportion of Karnataka's cropped area was occupied by cereals on average according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Cereals occupied 45% of total agricultural cropped area on average.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What proportion of Karnataka's cropped area was occupied by pulses on average according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Pulses occupied 28% of total agricultural cropped area on average.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What proportion of Karnataka's cropped area was occupied by oilseeds on average according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Oilseeds occupied 10% of total agricultural cropped area on average.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What proportion of Karnataka's cropped area was occupied by cotton on average according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Cotton occupied 7% of total agricultural cropped area on average.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What proportion of Karnataka's cropped area was occupied by sugarcane on average according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane occupied 9% of total agricultural cropped area on average.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What proportion of Karnataka's cropped area was occupied by tobacco on average according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Tobacco occupied 1% of total agricultural cropped area on average.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major structural challenge facing Karnataka agriculture?
questions.explanation: Major structural challenges include dependence on monsoon rainfall, recurring droughts and floods, uneven irrigation, small and fragmented holdings, groundwater stress, soil nutrient deficiencies, price volatility, rising input costs, post-harvest losses and uneven access to markets and technology.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the average size of operational holdings in Karnataka as per the Census?
questions.explanation: The average size of operational holdings was 1.36 hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many operational holdings were recorded in Karnataka as per the Census?
questions.explanation: The Census recorded 86.81 lakh operational holdings operating 118.05 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What percentage of operational holdings in Karnataka were small and marginal?
questions.explanation: Small and marginal holdings made up about 80% of holdings and operated 44% of the area.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major food crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major food crops include rice (paddy), ragi (finger millet), jowar (sorghum), maize, bajra (pearl millet), wheat and other millets and cereals.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major pulse crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major pulse crops include tur or pigeon pea (red gram), Bengal gram (chickpea), green gram, black gram, horse gram and cowpea.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major oilseed crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major oilseed crops include groundnut, sunflower, soybean, sesame, safflower and castor.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is an important commercial crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Important commercial crops include sugarcane, cotton, tobacco, coffee, arecanut, coconut, cashew, rubber and plantation crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are especially associated with the northern dry districts of Karnataka?

options.B: Jowar, bajra, tur, chickpea, sunflower, cotton and maize

questions.explanation: Jowar, bajra, tur, chickpea, sunflower, cotton, maize and other dryland crops are important in different parts of northern Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are important in the southern and central districts of Karnataka?

options.A: Ragi, paddy, maize, pulses, sugarcane, coconut, arecanut and mulberry

questions.explanation: Ragi, paddy, maize, pulses, sugarcane, coconut, arecanut, mulberry and a wide range of horticultural crops are grown according to local rainfall and irrigation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are important in the coastal and Malnad regions of Karnataka?

options.B: Paddy, arecanut, coconut, cashew, pepper, cardamom, ginger and turmeric

questions.explanation: Paddy, arecanut, coconut, cashew, pepper, cardamom, ginger, turmeric, banana and other plantation and horticultural crops are important in coastal and Malnad regions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crop is known as a staple millet of southern Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Ragi or finger millet is a major staple millet, particularly in the old Mysuru region and adjoining dry districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are popularly associated with the black-soil belt of northern Karnataka?

options.B: Jowar, cotton, tur and other dryland crops

questions.explanation: Jowar, cotton, tur and other dryland crops are important in the black-soil areas of northern Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are strongly associated with the Cauvery command area in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Paddy and sugarcane are important irrigated crops in parts of the Cauvery basin, especially in Mandya and adjoining districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crop is Karnataka particularly famous for in the coffee sector?
questions.explanation: Coffee, especially Arabica and Robusta, grown mainly in the Western Ghats districts of Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which are the principal coffee-growing districts of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan are the principal coffee-growing districts of Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which are the important sugarcane-growing areas of Karnataka?

options.B: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Mandya, Mysuru, Bidar and Kalaburagi
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Mandya, Mysuru, Bidar, Kalaburagi and parts of other irrigated districts are important sugarcane-growing areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are known for cotton cultivation in Karnataka?

options.B: Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Ballari, Raichur, Dharwad, Haveri, Gadag and other northern and central districts
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Cotton is important in parts of Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Ballari, Raichur, Dharwad, Haveri, Gadag and other northern and central districts.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are important for tur or pigeon pea cultivation in Karnataka?

options.B: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Yadgir, Raichur, Vijayapura and other districts of the northern dry belt
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Yadgir, Raichur, Vijayapura and other districts of the northern dry belt are important tur-growing areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops showed a higher trend in recent years according to the 2025-26 Survey?

options.B: Maize, tur, green gram, soybean and sugarcane

questions.explanation: Maize, tur, green gram, soybean and sugarcane showed a higher trend in recent years.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How much agricultural crop area was damaged due to excess rainfall and floods in 2025 according to a district joint survey?
questions.explanation: A district joint survey reported damage to 13.83 lakh hectares of agricultural crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts were majorly affected by crop losses due to excess rainfall and floods in 2025?

options.B: Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, Bidar, Yadgir and Gadag
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Major affected districts included Kalaburagi, Vijayapura, Bidar, Yadgir and Gadag.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops were among those affected by excess rainfall and floods in 2025?

options.B: Tur, green gram, cotton, maize and soybean

questions.explanation: Tur, green gram, cotton, maize and soybean were among the affected crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical Kharif crop in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Typical Kharif crops include paddy, ragi, jowar, maize, tur, green gram, soybean, groundnut and cotton.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the main feature of Kharif season in Karnataka?

options.A: Sown after monsoon with residual moisture
options.B: Sown with monsoon; rainfall-dependent in many areas
options.C: Usually depends more heavily on irrigation

questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon and are rainfall-dependent in many areas.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical Rabi crop in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Typical Rabi crops include jowar, chickpea, wheat, safflower, some pulses and oilseeds.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is important for Rabi crops in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Rabi crops are sown after monsoon; residual moisture and irrigation are important.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a typical Summer crop in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Typical Summer crops include paddy, maize, pulses, vegetables and fodder crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the main feature of Summer crops in Karnataka?

options.B: Usually depends more heavily on irrigation

questions.explanation: Summer crops usually depend more heavily on irrigation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is irrigation?

options.B: Artificial supply of water to agricultural land to support crop growth

questions.explanation: Irrigation is the artificial supply of water to agricultural land to support crop growth when rainfall is insufficient or irregular.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Why is irrigation important in Karnataka?

options.A: Because the state receives no rainfall
options.B: Because a large part of the State has semi-arid or drought-prone conditions
options.D: Because irrigation is cheaper than rainfall

questions.explanation: A large part of the State has semi-arid or drought-prone conditions. Irrigation stabilises yields, reduces monsoon dependence, supports high-value crops and enables multiple cropping.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which monsoon provides the major share of Karnataka's rainfall?
questions.explanation: The South-West Monsoon provides more than 73% of the State's annual rainfall according to the Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the annual average rainfall of Karnataka reported in the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: The annual average rainfall of Karnataka is 1,355 millimetres according to the 2025-26 Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which river basin has the largest drainage area in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Krishna basin has 58.93% of the State's drainage area according to the Survey's river-basin table.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which river basin has the second-largest drainage area in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Cauvery basin accounts for 18.84% of the State's drainage area in the Survey table.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major river basin associated with Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major river basins associated with Karnataka include Krishna, Cauvery, Godavari, North Pennar, South Pennar, Palar and the west-flowing river systems.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the ultimate irrigation potential under Major and Medium Irrigation Projects in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The ultimate irrigation potential under Major and Medium Irrigation Projects in Karnataka is 42.08 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How much irrigation potential had been achieved under Major and Medium Irrigation Projects by December 2025?
questions.explanation: 30.92 lakh hectares had been achieved by December 2025, leaving 11.16 lakh hectares yet to be achieved.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How much irrigation potential remained to be achieved under Major and Medium Irrigation Projects by December 2025?
questions.explanation: 11.16 lakh hectares remained yet to be achieved according to the 2025-26 Economic Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major type of irrigation in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major types of irrigation include canal irrigation, tank irrigation, well and borewell irrigation, lift irrigation, drip irrigation and sprinkler irrigation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is canal irrigation?

options.B: Conveying water from rivers or reservoirs through an engineered network of canals
options.D: Supplying water directly to roots through emitters

questions.explanation: Canal irrigation conveys water from rivers or reservoirs through an engineered network of main canals, branch canals and field channels to agricultural land.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is tank irrigation?

options.B: Storing rainwater or runoff in tanks and distributing it to nearby fields

questions.explanation: Tank irrigation stores rainwater or runoff in tanks and distributes it to nearby agricultural fields; tanks also help recharge groundwater.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is lift irrigation?

options.B: Using pumps to raise water from rivers or reservoirs to higher elevation fields

questions.explanation: Lift irrigation uses pumps to raise water from rivers, reservoirs or other sources to fields situated at a higher elevation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is drip irrigation?

options.A: Flooding the entire field with water
options.B: Supplying water slowly and directly near the plant root zone through emitters

questions.explanation: Drip irrigation supplies water slowly and directly near the plant root zone through emitters and pipes, reducing evaporation and conveyance losses.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is sprinkler irrigation?

options.B: Distributing water through pressurised pipes and spray nozzles simulating rainfall

questions.explanation: Sprinkler irrigation distributes water through pressurised pipes and spray nozzles, simulating rainfall over crops.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which irrigation method is generally most water-efficient for orchards and row crops?
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation is generally highly water-efficient when properly designed and maintained because it applies water close to the root zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the difference between irrigation potential created and irrigation potential utilised?

options.B: Potential created is the area infrastructure can irrigate; potential utilised is the area actually irrigated
options.C: Potential created is always less than utilised
options.D: Potential utilised is the area that can be irrigated; created is the area actually irrigated

questions.explanation: Potential created is the area that infrastructure is capable of irrigating; potential utilised is the area actually irrigated during a specified period. They are not the same.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the objective of the Water Resources Department regarding irrigation potential?

options.B: To harness surface water for irrigation, drinking and industrial purposes and work towards 42.08 lakh hectares
options.C: To focus only on drinking water

questions.explanation: The objective is to harness surface water for irrigation, drinking and industrial purposes and work towards the State's ultimate irrigation potential of 42.08 lakh hectares through major and medium projects.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the Krishi Bhagya scheme intended to do?

options.B: Support rainfed farmers through farm ponds and water-conservation measures

questions.explanation: Krishi Bhagya supports rainfed farmers through farm ponds and related water-conservation and protective-irrigation measures to improve resilience in dryland agriculture.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many farm ponds were constructed under Krishi Bhagya-related allocations by December 2025?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reports 4,529 farm ponds constructed up to December 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the micro-irrigation achievement reported for the agriculture department in 2025-26 up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: Micro-irrigation coverage reached 1,00,956 hectares under the programme.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the micro-irrigation coverage reported for horticulture under PM-RKVY up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: Micro-irrigation coverage for horticulture under PM-RKVY was 30,653.66 hectares, benefiting 35,021 farmers through subsidies of 246.66 crore.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many farmers benefited from micro-irrigation under PM-RKVY for horticulture up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: 35,021 farmers benefited through subsidies of 246.66 crore.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major irrigation challenge in Karnataka?

options.B: Uneven distribution of water and inter-state river disputes

questions.explanation: Major irrigation challenges include uneven distribution of water, inter-state river disputes, droughts, groundwater depletion, inefficient flood irrigation, incomplete projects, waterlogging and salinity in some command areas, and high costs of energy and infrastructure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many agro-climatic zones has Karnataka traditionally been divided into?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has traditionally been divided into ten agro-climatic zones based on rainfall distribution, soil, altitude and cropping pattern.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which institution has been entrusted with technical work to redefine Karnataka's agro-climatic zones?

options.B: Karnataka State Remote Sensing Applications Centre (KSRsAC), Bengaluru

questions.explanation: Karnataka State Remote Sensing Applications Centre (KSRsAC), Bengaluru, with technical support from other institutions, has been entrusted with this work.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is one of the ten traditional agro-climatic zones of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The ten traditional agro-climatic zones include North Eastern Transition Zone; North Eastern Dry Zone; Northern Dry Zone; Central Dry Zone; Eastern Dry Zone; Southern Dry Zone; Southern Transition Zone; Northern Transition Zone; Hilly Zone; and Coastal Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the North Eastern Transition Zone of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Bidar and parts of Kalaburagi (formerly Gulbarga) broadly fall in the North Eastern Transition Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the North Eastern Dry Zone of Karnataka?

options.B: Parts of Kalaburagi, Yadgir and Raichur

questions.explanation: Parts of Kalaburagi, Yadgir and Raichur broadly fall in the North Eastern Dry Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Northern Dry Zone of Karnataka?

options.A: Parts of Koppal, Gadag, Dharwad, Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Ballari, Davanagere and Raichur

questions.explanation: Parts of Koppal, Gadag, Dharwad, Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Ballari, Davanagere and Raichur broadly fall in the Northern Dry Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Central Dry Zone of Karnataka?

options.B: Chitradurga, parts of Davanagere, Tumakuru, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan

questions.explanation: Chitradurga, parts of Davanagere, Tumakuru, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan broadly fall in the Central Dry Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Eastern Dry Zone of Karnataka?

options.A: Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Kolar, Chikkaballapur and parts of Tumakuru

questions.explanation: Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Kolar, Chikkaballapur and parts of Tumakuru broadly fall in the Eastern Dry Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Southern Dry Zone of Karnataka?

options.B: Mysuru, Chamarajanagar, Mandya and parts of Tumakuru and Hassan

questions.explanation: Mysuru, Chamarajanagar, Mandya and parts of Tumakuru and Hassan broadly fall in the Southern Dry Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Northern Transition Zone of Karnataka?

options.A: Parts of Belagavi, Dharwad, Haveri and Gadag

questions.explanation: Parts of Belagavi, Dharwad, Haveri and Gadag broadly fall in the Northern Transition Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Hilly Zone of Karnataka?

options.A: Uttara Kannada, parts of Belagavi, Dharwad, Haveri, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu and Hassan

questions.explanation: Uttara Kannada, parts of Belagavi, Dharwad, Haveri, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu and Hassan broadly fall in the Hilly Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts broadly fall in the Coastal Zone of Karnataka?

options.A: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and coastal parts of Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and coastal parts of Uttara Kannada broadly fall in the Coastal Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are common in the Northern Dry Zone of Karnataka?

options.B: Jowar, bajra, tur, chickpea, sunflower, cotton and other dryland crops

questions.explanation: Jowar, bajra, tur, chickpea, sunflower, cotton and other dryland crops are common in the Northern Dry Zone.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.chapter: Southern and Eastern Dry Zones Crops
questions.question: Which crops are common in the Southern Dry and Eastern Dry Zones of Karnataka?

options.B: Ragi, groundnut, pulses, maize, mulberry and dryland horticultural crops

questions.explanation: Ragi, groundnut, pulses, maize, mulberry and dryland horticultural crops are common; irrigated pockets also grow paddy and sugarcane.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which crops are common in the Hilly and Coastal Zones of Karnataka?

options.B: Paddy, arecanut, coconut, coffee, pepper, cardamom, cashew, ginger and turmeric

questions.explanation: Paddy, arecanut, coconut, coffee, pepper, cardamom, cashew, ginger, turmeric and other plantation crops are common in the Hilly and Coastal Zones.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are especially associated with coffee cultivation in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Hassan are especially associated with coffee cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are especially associated with arecanut cultivation in Karnataka?

options.A: Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Davanagere, Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada and parts of Hassan

questions.explanation: Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Davanagere, Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada and parts of Hassan are especially associated with arecanut cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are especially associated with ragi cultivation in Karnataka?

options.A: Mandya, Mysuru, Ramanagara, Bengaluru Rural, Chikkaballapur, Kolar, Tumakuru and Chitradurga
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Mandya, Mysuru, Ramanagara, Bengaluru Rural, Chikkaballapur, Kolar, Tumakuru and Chitradurga are especially associated with ragi cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are especially associated with sugarcane cultivation in Karnataka?

options.A: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Mandya, Mysuru, Vijayapura and parts of Bidar and Kalaburagi
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Mandya, Mysuru, Vijayapura and parts of Bidar and Kalaburagi are especially associated with sugarcane cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is horticulture?

options.B: Branch of agriculture concerned with fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops, medicinal and aromatic plants

questions.explanation: Horticulture is the branch of agriculture concerned with the cultivation, production, management and marketing of fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops, medicinal and aromatic plants.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What does horticulture provide to farmers?

options.B: Higher-value crop options, diversified farm income, processing and export support

questions.explanation: Horticulture provides higher-value crop options, diversifies farm income, supports processing and exports, creates rural employment and can be suitable for several dryland and irrigated agro-climatic regions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major fruit crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major fruit crops include mango, banana, grapes, pomegranate, citrus, guava, sapota, papaya, pineapple, jackfruit and watermelon.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major vegetable crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major vegetable crops include tomato, onion, potato, chilli, brinjal, cabbage, cauliflower, beans, carrot, cucumber and okra.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is an important spice crop grown in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Important spice crops include chilli, pepper, cardamom, ginger, turmeric, coriander and other spices.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is an important plantation crop of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Important plantation and garden crops include arecanut, coconut, coffee, cashew, cocoa, rubber and oil palm.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are known for grape cultivation in Karnataka?

options.B: Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Belagavi, Koppal and parts of Bengaluru Rural
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Belagavi, Koppal and parts of Bengaluru Rural and other suitable districts are known for grape cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are known for mango cultivation in Karnataka?

options.A: Kolar, Ramanagara, Chikkaballapur, Bengaluru Rural and Dharwad
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Kolar, Ramanagara, Chikkaballapur, Bengaluru Rural, Dharwad and other districts are known for mango cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are important for pomegranate cultivation in Karnataka?

options.B: Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Belagavi, Koppal and other northern dry districts
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Belagavi, Koppal and other northern dry districts are important for pomegranate cultivation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are important for tomato production in Karnataka?

options.B: Kolar, Chikkaballapur, Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru Urban and other vegetable-growing districts
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Kolar, Chikkaballapur, Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru Urban and other vegetable-growing districts are important for tomato production.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What are protected cultivation methods in horticulture?

options.B: Polythouses, greenhouses, shade-net houses and other structures that modify the crop environment

questions.explanation: Protected cultivation includes polythouses, greenhouses, shade-net houses and other structures that modify the crop environment to improve quality, productivity and resource-use efficiency.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is precision horticulture?

options.B: Using sensors, data, targeted irrigation, fertigation, remote sensing and other technologies to manage crops accurately

questions.explanation: Precision horticulture uses sensors, data, targeted irrigation, fertigation, remote sensing and other technologies to manage crops and inputs accurately.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is post-harvest management in horticulture?

options.B: Cleaning, grading, sorting, packaging, pre-cooling, storage, cold-chain transport, processing and marketing after harvest

questions.explanation: Post-harvest management includes cleaning, grading, sorting, packaging, pre-cooling, storage, cold-chain transport, processing and marketing after harvest to reduce losses and maintain quality.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is apiculture?

options.B: Scientific rearing and management of honeybees

questions.explanation: Apiculture is the scientific rearing and management of honeybees for honey, wax and other products, as well as for pollination services.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many grafts and seedlings were produced in Karnataka in 2025-26 up to December against a target of 70.80 lakh?
questions.explanation: The Survey reports 26.95 lakh grafts and seedlings produced against a target of 70.80 lakh; 43.60 lakh were available for sale.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many grafts and seedlings were available for sale in Karnataka in 2025-26 up to December?
questions.explanation: 43.60 lakh grafts and seedlings were available for sale.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many beneficiaries were trained under the apiculture programme up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: 859 beneficiaries were trained under the apiculture programme up to December 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many honey boxes were distributed under the apiculture programme up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: 7,245 honey boxes were distributed under the apiculture programme.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many Madhuvanas were established under the apiculture programme up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: 17 Madhuvanas were established under the apiculture programme.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many honey extractors were supported under the apiculture programme up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: 48 honey extractors were supported under the apiculture programme.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the purpose of horticulture cold-storage infrastructure?

options.B: To slow deterioration, reduce post-harvest losses and maintain quality

questions.explanation: Cold storage slows deterioration, reduces post-harvest losses, allows better timing of sales and helps maintain quality and market value of perishable produce.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major constraint in horticulture?
questions.explanation: Major constraints include perishability, inadequate cold chains, price fluctuations, pest and disease risks, water scarcity, fragmented production, quality standards and limited processing or market access in some regions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is sericulture?

options.B: Scientific cultivation of mulberry and rearing of silkworms for silk cocoons and raw silk

questions.explanation: Sericulture is the scientific cultivation of mulberry or other host plants and rearing of silkworms for the production of silk cocoons and raw silk.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which silkworm is most widely used in Karnataka's mulberry sericulture?
questions.explanation: The mulberry silkworm, Bombyx mori, is most widely used in Karnataka's mulberry sericulture.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which plant is the principal food plant for the mulberry silkworm?
questions.explanation: Mulberry (Morus species) is the principal food plant for the mulberry silkworm.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Why is Karnataka important in Indian sericulture?

options.B: It is one of India's leading silk-producing States with a long-established ecosystem

questions.explanation: Karnataka is one of India's leading silk-producing States and has a long-established mulberry cultivation, cocoon-rearing, reeling, weaving and silk-marketing ecosystem.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which districts are important for sericulture in Karnataka?

options.A: Ramanagara, Chikkaballapur, Kolar, Bengaluru Rural, Mandya, Mysuru and Tumakuru
options.C: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada and Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Ramanagara, Chikkaballapur, Kolar, Bengaluru Rural, Mandya, Mysuru, Tumakuru and other southern districts are important for sericulture.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which market is particularly famous for silk cocoons in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Ramanagara is a major cocoon market; Shidlaghatta is another important silk-market centre.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was Karnataka's mulberry silk production in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's mulberry silk production in 2024-25 was 13,276.64 metric tonnes according to the Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the area under mulberry cultivation in Karnataka at the end of December 2025?
questions.explanation: The area under mulberry cultivation was 1,22,939 hectares at the end of December 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What overall allocation was provided for sericulture development in 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The overall allocation for sericulture development in 2025-26 was 487.059 crore, including State and District Sector schemes, PMKSY assistance and the Silk Samagra central-sector scheme.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is bivoltine silk?

options.A: Silk produced by silkworms that complete one generation in a year
options.B: Silk produced by silkworm races that complete two generations in a year, generally finer and stronger
options.C: Silk produced only in coastal areas

questions.explanation: Bivoltine silk is produced by silkworm races that complete two generations (broods) in a year; it is generally associated with finer, stronger and higher-quality silk, though it requires suitable rearing conditions.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of stages in silk production?

options.A: Reeling, mulberry cultivation, cocoon formation, weaving
options.B: Mulberry cultivation, silkworm rearing, cocoon formation, reeling, weaving
options.C: Weaving, reeling, cocoon formation, mulberry cultivation
options.D: Cocoon formation, mulberry cultivation, reeling, weaving

questions.explanation: The main stages are: mulberry cultivation; silkworm egg incubation; silkworm rearing; cocoon formation and harvesting; cocoon drying or stifling; reeling; twisting; weaving; dyeing and finishing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is silk reeling?

options.B: Process of unwinding continuous silk filaments from cocoons to produce raw silk yarn

questions.explanation: Silk reeling is the process of unwinding continuous silk filaments from cocoons and combining them to produce raw silk yarn.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major benefit of sericulture?

options.B: Generates rural employment, supplementary income and supports women's livelihoods

questions.explanation: Sericulture generates rural employment, provides supplementary income, supports women's livelihoods, encourages small-scale enterprise and supplies raw material to silk-based textile industries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major problem faced by sericulture?

options.B: Silkworm disease and fluctuating cocoon prices

questions.explanation: Major problems include silkworm disease, fluctuating cocoon prices, quality variation, high labour requirements, climate sensitivity, input costs, competition from imported silk and the need for modern reeling and market infrastructure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is dairy farming?

options.B: Rearing and management of milch animals for milk and milk products

questions.explanation: Dairy farming is the rearing and management of milch animals for the production and sale of milk and milk products.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Why is dairy important to Karnataka's rural economy?

options.B: It provides regular cash income, employment, nutrition and reduces risk from crop failure

questions.explanation: Dairy provides regular cash income, creates employment, supports nutrition, diversifies farm income and can reduce the risk associated with crop failure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which organisation is the apex cooperative dairy federation in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Karnataka Co-operative Milk Producers' Federation Limited (KMF) is the apex cooperative dairy federation in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which brand is marketed by Karnataka Milk Federation?
questions.explanation: Nandini is the brand marketed by Karnataka Milk Federation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: When was the Karnataka Dairy Development Corporation established?
questions.explanation: The Karnataka Dairy Development Corporation was established in 1974 with World Bank assistance under Operation Flood-I; later evolved into the Karnataka Milk Federation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the three-tier structure of Karnataka's dairy cooperative system?

options.A: Village societies, district unions, state federation
options.B: State government, district panchayat, village panchayat

questions.explanation: The three-tier structure consists of Village-level Primary Milk Producers' Cooperative Societies; district-level Milk Unions; and the State-level Karnataka Co-operative Milk Producers' Federation (KMF).

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many District Milk Unions are there in Karnataka's dairy cooperative system?
questions.explanation: There are 16 District Milk Unions in Karnataka's dairy cooperative system.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many Primary Milk Producers' Cooperative Societies are there in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: There are 16,142 Primary Milk Producers' Cooperative Societies, including 4,813 women's milk cooperative societies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many women's milk cooperative societies are there in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: There are 4,813 women's milk cooperative societies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many milk producer members were reported in the KMF network?
questions.explanation: 27.19 lakh members were reported, of whom 9.06 lakh were active members, according to the 2025-26 Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many active members were reported in the KMF network?
questions.explanation: 9.06 lakh active members were reported in the KMF network according to the 2025-26 Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was Karnataka's milk production in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's milk production in 2024-25 was 13.89 million metric tonnes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the average daily milk procurement by KMF during 2025-26 as reported in the Survey?
questions.explanation: The average daily milk procurement by KMF during 2025-26 was approximately 1 crore litres per day.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was KMF's record peak daily milk procurement in 2025?
questions.explanation: KMF's record peak daily milk procurement was 106.54 lakh litres on 21 June 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the milk incentive provided by the Karnataka Government to eligible milk producers?
questions.explanation: The State provides an incentive of 5 per litre for the supply of quality milk, transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer after verification.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the Ksheerabhagya scheme?

options.B: A nutrition programme supplying free milk powder to schoolchildren and Anganwadi children

questions.explanation: Ksheerabhagya is a Karnataka Government nutrition programme under which milk powder is supplied free of cost five days a week to schoolchildren in Classes I to X and children attending Anganwadi centres.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many children benefit from Ksheerabhagya according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: More than one crore children benefit from Ksheerabhagya according to the 2025-26 Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is artificial insemination in dairy development?

options.B: Controlled introduction of semen into a female animal's reproductive tract to improve breeding and genetics

questions.explanation: Artificial insemination is the controlled introduction of semen into a female animal's reproductive tract to improve breeding, genetics and herd productivity.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the purpose of sex-sorted semen?

options.B: To increase the probability of producing calves of a desired sex, commonly female calves in dairy

questions.explanation: Sex-sorted semen increases the probability of producing calves of a desired sex; in dairy systems it is commonly used to increase the proportion of female calves.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many Automatic Milk Collection Unit (AMCU) units were reported in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Survey reports 12,985 Automatic Milk Collection Unit (AMCU) units.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many Bulk Milk Coolers were reported in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Survey reports 2,324 Bulk Milk Coolers.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many milk processing plants are there in Karnataka with combined processing capacity of 1.37 crore litres per day?
questions.explanation: The Survey reports 45 milk processing plants with combined processing capacity of 1.37 crore litres per day.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Bulk Milk Cooler (BMC)?

options.B: To rapidly cool collected milk to slow bacterial growth and preserve quality

questions.explanation: A Bulk Milk Cooler rapidly cools collected milk at or near the village collection point to slow bacterial growth and preserve quality before transport to a processing plant.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major dairy challenge in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major dairy challenges include fodder shortages, feed costs, animal diseases, heat stress, low productivity in some herds, uneven veterinary access, milk price fluctuations and the need for stronger chilling and processing infrastructure.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What does fisheries include?

options.B: Catching, culture, processing and marketing of fish and other aquatic organisms

questions.explanation: Fisheries includes the catching, culture, processing and marketing of fish and other aquatic organisms from marine, inland and brackish-water resources.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What are the two broad types of fisheries in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The two broad types are marine fisheries along the Arabian Sea coast and inland fisheries in rivers, reservoirs, lakes, tanks, ponds and other freshwater bodies.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is aquaculture?

options.B: Controlled cultivation of fish, shellfish, aquatic plants and other aquatic organisms

questions.explanation: Aquaculture is the controlled cultivation of fish, shellfish, aquatic plants and other aquatic organisms in freshwater, brackish-water or marine environments.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is mariculture?

options.B: Aquaculture practised in seawater or marine environments

questions.explanation: Mariculture is aquaculture practised in seawater or marine environments.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is brackish-water aquaculture?

options.B: Farming in water with salinity between freshwater and seawater

questions.explanation: Brackish-water aquaculture is the farming of aquatic organisms in water with salinity between freshwater and seawater, often in estuaries, creeks and coastal ponds.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the length of Karnataka's coastline according to the 2025-26 Economic Survey?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's coastline is 320 kilometres according to the 2025-26 Economic Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the continental shelf area associated with Karnataka in the Survey?
questions.explanation: The continental shelf area associated with Karnataka is 27,000 square kilometres.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the inland water resource area reported for Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The inland water resource area reported for Karnataka is 5.83 lakh hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the brackish-water area reported for Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The brackish-water area reported for Karnataka is about 8,000 hectares.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many people were engaged in fisheries activities in Karnataka according to the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: About 9.84 lakh fishermen were engaged, including 3.31 lakh in marine fisheries and 6.53 lakh in inland fisheries.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was Karnataka's total fish production in 2024-25?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's total fish production in 2024-25 was 9.63 lakh metric tonnes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was fish production in Karnataka in 2025-26 up to the end of December 2025?
questions.explanation: Fish production in 2025-26 up to December 2025 was 6.59 lakh metric tonnes.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the fisheries sector's share in Karnataka's GSDP in the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: The fisheries sector's share in Karnataka's GSDP was 0.48 per cent in the 2025-26 Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many fishing boats were engaged in marine fishing in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: 25,246 boats were engaged: 4,828 mechanised boats, 11,443 motorised boats, 8,953 traditional boats and 22 deep-sea fishing vessels.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many motorised boats were engaged in marine fishing in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: There were 11,443 motorised boats engaged in marine fishing in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many traditional boats were engaged in marine fishing in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: There were 8,953 traditional boats engaged in marine fishing in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many fish seed production centres were reported in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: 16 fish seed production centres were reported in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was fish seed production in 2025-26 up to December 2025?
questions.explanation: Fish seed production was 6,311.50 lakh fry-size fish seeds against a target of 10,000 lakh.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)?

options.B: A flagship scheme for sustainable development of fisheries including production, aquaculture, infrastructure and marketing

questions.explanation: PMMSY is a Government of India flagship scheme for sustainable and responsible development of fisheries, including production, aquaculture, infrastructure, post-harvest management, value addition and marketing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is a Fish Farmer Producer Organisation (FFPO)?

options.B: A collective institution of fishers or fish farmers for input access, production, aggregation and marketing

questions.explanation: An FFPO is a collective institution of fishers or fish farmers formed to improve input access, production, aggregation, processing, bargaining power and marketing.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many Fish Farmer Producer Organisations were reported as registered in Karnataka by the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: 62 Fish Farmer Producer Organisations were reported as registered in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which of the following is a major fisheries challenge in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Major fisheries challenges include monsoon-related fishing restrictions, cyclones and rough seas, declining or variable fish stocks, ageing boats, safety at sea, inadequate cold chains, post-harvest losses, limited processing capacity and environmental degradation.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is agricultural marketing?

options.B: Activities involved in moving farm produce from producers to consumers including assembling, grading, storage, transport, processing, price discovery, sale and payment

questions.explanation: Agricultural marketing covers the activities involved in moving farm produce from producers to consumers, including assembling, grading, storage, transport, processing, price discovery, sale and payment.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Why is agricultural marketing important?

options.B: It reduces transaction costs and post-harvest losses and helps farmers obtain remunerative prices

questions.explanation: Efficient marketing reduces transaction costs and post-harvest losses, improves price discovery, expands market access and helps farmers obtain remunerative prices.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is an Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC)?

options.B: A statutory market-regulating institution established under State agricultural marketing law

questions.explanation: An APMC is a statutory market-regulating institution established under State agricultural marketing law to regulate notified agricultural produce markets and trading activities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many APMCs were reported in Karnataka in the 2025-26 Economic Survey?
questions.explanation: 170 APMCs were reported in Karnataka in the 2025-26 Economic Survey.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is Rashtriya e-Market Services Limited (ReMS)?

options.B: A special purpose vehicle established to implement agricultural marketing reforms and electronic trading

questions.explanation: ReMS is a special purpose vehicle established to implement agricultural marketing reforms and electronic trading through Karnataka's Unified Market Platform.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: When was ReMS established?
questions.explanation: ReMS was established on 20 January 2014.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the Unified Market Platform (UMP)?

options.B: Karnataka's electronic agricultural trading platform that links regulated markets and supports online bidding and electronic payment

questions.explanation: UMP is Karnataka's electronic agricultural trading platform that links regulated markets and supports online bidding, transparent price discovery and electronic payment.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: How many APMCs were linked to the Unified Market Platform by December 2025?
questions.explanation: 167 APMCs were linked to the Unified Market Platform by December 2025.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which Karnataka APMCs were linked to the Government of India's e-NAM platform as stated in the 2025-26 Survey?
questions.explanation: Kalaburagi and Chincholi APMCs were linked to the Government of India's e-NAM platform.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What was the cumulative transaction volume and value of the Unified Market Platform by December 2025?
questions.explanation: The cumulative transaction volume and value of the UMP by December 2025 was 12.67 crore metric tonnes of agricultural commodities valued at 4,39,852.54 crore.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is e-NAM?

options.B: National Agriculture Market - a pan-India electronic trading portal

questions.explanation: The National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) is a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks APMC mandis to create a more integrated national market for agricultural commodities.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is Minimum Support Price (MSP)?

options.A: A price announced by the Government of India for selected crops to provide price assurance

questions.explanation: MSP is a price announced by the Government of India for selected agricultural commodities to provide price assurance to farmers; procurement at MSP depends on notified crops, agencies, quality norms and operational arrangements.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the difference between MSP and Karnataka's Minimum Floor Price scheme?

options.B: MSP is announced by the Union Government; Karnataka's Minimum Floor Price is a State-level intervention
options.C: MSP is a state scheme; Minimum Floor Price is central

questions.explanation: MSP is announced by the Union Government for notified crops. Karnataka's Minimum Floor Price scheme is a State-level intervention for notified agricultural and horticultural commodities when market prices fall sharply, with the aim of protecting farmers from distress sales.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is the Price Support Scheme?

options.B: A Government of India procurement intervention for notified crops when market prices fall below MSP

questions.explanation: It is a Government of India procurement intervention for notified crops, implemented through designated agencies when market prices fall below MSP and prescribed conditions are met.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: Which commodities were procured under Karnataka's support-price scheme during 2025-26 as reported in the Survey?

options.B: Green gram, urad dal, sunflower, soybean, groundnut, maize and cotton

questions.explanation: Green gram, urad dal, sunflower, soybean, groundnut, maize and cotton were among the listed commodities; the Survey reports procurement from 1,55,793 registered farmers up to the reporting period.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is grading of agricultural produce?

options.A: Classification of produce according to defined quality parameters

questions.explanation: Grading is the classification of produce according to defined quality parameters such as size, weight, colour, moisture, purity and defects.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is assaying in agricultural markets?

options.B: Testing of a commodity's quality and composition against specified standards

questions.explanation: Assaying is the testing of a commodity's quality and composition against specified standards to support reliable grading and fair price discovery.

questions.subject: Karnataka Agriculture
questions.question: What is a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)?

options.B: A farmer-owned collective enterprise that aggregates produce and improves bargaining power

questions.explanation: An FPO is a farmer-owned collective enterprise that aggregates produce and inputs, improves bargaining power, enables economies of scale and supports processing and marketing.
